name: The four establishments of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhāna)
method_summary: Abiding contemplating the body in the body, feelings in feelings, mind in mind and dhammas in dhammas, ardent, clearly comprehending and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief; each contemplated internally, externally and both, as arising and passing, until mindfulness is established just for knowledge, independent and clinging to nothing (MN 10; DN 22).
signs_of_progress: one of two fruits: final knowledge here and now or non-return, within seven years down to seven days (MN 10)

equivalents.note: the same four contemplations as systematised in the Sarvāstivāda Abhidharmakośa (U38)

name: Contemplation of the body (kāyānupassanā)
method_summary: Mindfulness of breathing, the postures, clear comprehension, the parts of the body, the elements and the charnel-ground stages (MN 10; MN 119).

name: Contemplation of feelings (vedanānupassanā)
method_summary: Knowing pleasant, painful and neutral feelings as they are, worldly or unworldly (MN 10); feeling only the first dart (SN 36.6).

name: Contemplation of mind (cittānupassanā)
method_summary: Knowing the mind as with or without lust, hatred, delusion, contracted, scattered, exalted, concentrated, liberated (MN 10).

name: Contemplation of dhammas (dhammānupassanā)
method_summary: Contemplating the hindrances, the aggregates, the sense bases and their fetters, the factors of awakening and the four truths (MN 10; DN 22).

name: Mindfulness directed to the body (kāyagatāsati)
method_summary: Developing the body contemplations of MN 10 together with the four jhānas as pervasions of the body (MN 119); like a bowl of oil carried through a crowd (SN 47.20), the post to which the six senses are tied (SN 35.247).
signs_of_progress: ten benefits: conquering discontent and fear, enduring pain, the jhānas at will, the direct knowledges, the destruction of the effluents (MN 119)

name: Mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasati)
method_summary: Seated in a secluded place, body erect, mindfulness established, one breathes in and out mindfully through sixteen steps in four tetrads — body, feeling, mind, dhammas — which fulfil the establishments of mindfulness, the factors of awakening, and true knowledge and liberation (MN 118; SN 54.1); the natural breath is known, not controlled.
signs_of_progress: the final breaths known as they cease (MN 62)
unwholesome states dispersed like dust by rain (SN 54.9)

warnings.text: I do not say there is development of mindfulness of breathing for one who is muddled and not clearly comprehending.

equivalents.note: both take the breath as object, but ānāpānasati observes the natural breath without retention; not the same practice

name: Ānāpānasati step 1: long breath (dīghaṁ assasāmī)
method_summary: Breathing in long, he knows 'I breathe in long'; breathing out long, he knows 'I breathe out long'. Step 1 of the sixteen; in the body tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of body (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 2: short breath (rassaṁ assasāmī)
method_summary: Breathing in short, he knows 'I breathe in short'; breathing out short, he knows it. Step 2 of the sixteen; in the body tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of body (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 3: experiencing the whole body (sabbakāyapaṭisaṁvedī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) experiencing the whole body'. Step 3 of the sixteen; in the body tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of body (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 4: calming the bodily formation (passambhayaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) calming the bodily formation'. Step 4 of the sixteen; in the body tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of body (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 5: experiencing rapture (pītipaṭisaṁvedī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) experiencing rapture'. Step 5 of the sixteen; in the feelings tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of feelings (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 6: experiencing bliss (sukhapaṭisaṁvedī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) experiencing bliss'. Step 6 of the sixteen; in the feelings tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of feelings (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 7: experiencing the mental formation (cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṁvedī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) experiencing the mental formation' (perception and feeling). Step 7 of the sixteen; in the feelings tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of feelings (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 8: calming the mental formation (passambhayaṁ cittasaṅkhāraṁ)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) calming the mental formation'. Step 8 of the sixteen; in the feelings tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of feelings (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 9: experiencing the mind (cittapaṭisaṁvedī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) experiencing the mind'. Step 9 of the sixteen; in the mind tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of mind (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 10: gladdening the mind (abhippamodayaṁ cittaṁ)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) gladdening the mind'. Step 10 of the sixteen; in the mind tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of mind (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 11: concentrating the mind (samādahaṁ cittaṁ)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) concentrating the mind'. Step 11 of the sixteen; in the mind tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of mind (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 12: liberating the mind (vimocayaṁ cittaṁ)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) liberating the mind'. Step 12 of the sixteen; in the mind tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of mind (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 13: contemplating impermanence (aniccānupassī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) contemplating impermanence'. Step 13 of the sixteen; in the dhammas tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of dhammas (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 14: contemplating fading away (virāgānupassī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) contemplating fading away (dispassion)'. Step 14 of the sixteen; in the dhammas tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of dhammas (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 15: contemplating cessation (nirodhānupassī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) contemplating cessation'. Step 15 of the sixteen; in the dhammas tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of dhammas (MN 118).

name: Ānāpānasati step 16: contemplating relinquishment (paṭinissaggānupassī)
method_summary: He trains: 'I shall breathe in (out) contemplating relinquishment'. Step 16 of the sixteen; in the dhammas tetrad, which fulfils the establishment of mindfulness of dhammas (MN 118).

name: Clear comprehension (sampajañña)
method_summary: Acting with full awareness in going and returning, looking, bending and stretching, wearing robes, eating, excreting, walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking and keeping silent (DN 2; MN 10).

name: Mindfulness of the postures
method_summary: Knowing 'I am walking', 'standing', 'sitting', 'lying down' however the body is disposed (MN 10; MN 119).

name: Reflection on the parts of the body (paṭikūlamanasikāra)
method_summary: Reviewing the body from the soles up and the hair down as full of impurities — the thirty-one/thirty-two parts — like a bag of mixed grains (MN 10; Khp 3); counters lust (MN 62).

warnings.text: After the Buddha praised the meditation on foulness, monks at Vesālī practising it became disgusted with their bodies and some took their lives; he then taught mindfulness of breathing as peaceful and sublime.

name: Reflection on the elements (dhātumanasikāra)
method_summary: Reviewing the body as earth, water, fire and air (and space), internal and external, like a butcher's carcass cut into pieces, seen as 'not mine, not I, not my self'; meditating like the earth that is unaffected by what is thrown on it (MN 10; MN 28; MN 62; MN 140).

name: The nine charnel-ground contemplations
method_summary: Comparing one's body with a corpse in its stages of decay — bloated, devoured, skeleton with flesh, without flesh, bones scattered, bleached, heaped, crumbled — 'this body too is of that nature' (MN 10; MN 119).
notes: A contemplation (imagined or seen); the texts do not prescribe any bodily act. Charnel-ground dwelling appears among the ascetic practices (see prc:dhutanga).

name: Meditation on foulness (asubha)
method_summary: Attending to the unattractiveness of the body (the parts, the corpse) to abandon lust (MN 62; Ud 4.1); one of the ten perceptions (AN 10.60).

warnings.text: Monks at Vesālī who practised foulness became repelled by their own bodies and many took their lives or had others kill them; the Buddha laid down the third pārājika and taught mindfulness of breathing as a peaceful, sublime dwelling.

equivalents.note: Nyāya also prescribes the perception of the body's foulness against attachment

name: Mindfulness of death (maraṇassati)
method_summary: Reflecting that death may come at any moment — 'may I live for the time of one breath, to attend to the teaching' — and examining whether unwholesome states remain unabandoned, striving as one whose turban is on fire (AN 6.19–20); 'I am subject to death' (AN 5.57).
signs_of_progress: it merges in the deathless and culminates in the deathless (AN 6.19)

warnings.text: Those who develop it thinking 'may I live a day' or 'a meal' dwell negligently.

name: The five subjects for frequent reflection
method_summary: Reflecting often: I am subject to ageing, to illness, to death; I will be separated from all that is dear; I am the owner of my deeds (AN 5.57).

name: Contemplation of the aggregates
method_summary: Seeing each aggregate, past, future, present, internal or external, 'this is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self' (SN 22.59), and as foam, bubble, mirage, plantain, illusion (SN 22.95); contemplating their arising and passing (MN 10; AN 4.41).

name: Dwelling in emptiness (suññatāvihāra)
method_summary: Attending to a single perception (forest, earth, the formless spheres, the signless), seeing what is absent as empty and what remains as present, until the mind is freed (MN 121); dwelling in emptiness internally by not attending to signs (MN 122).

name: Perception of light
method_summary: Attending to the perception of light, resolving on 'day' by night as by day, with an open mind — a development of concentration leading to knowledge and vision (AN 4.41); a remedy for drowsiness (AN 7.61).

name: The kasiṇas
method_summary: Perceiving a totality — earth, water, fire, air, blue, yellow, red, white, space or consciousness — above, below, across, non-dual and immeasurable (AN 10.25); the commentaries build forty meditation subjects on them (U37).

name: Development of the four divine abidings
method_summary: Abiding pervading one direction, then the second, third and fourth, above, below, across and everywhere, with a mind of love, compassion, rejoicing and equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity (DN 13; MN 7; AN 3.65).

equivalents.note: YS 1.33 prescribes the four attitudes towards the happy, the suffering, the virtuous and the non-virtuous for clarity of mind

name: Development of loving-kindness (mettā)
method_summary: Cultivating a boundless heart towards all beings as a mother protects her only child, wishing 'may all beings be happy', standing, walking, sitting or lying down (Snp 1.8); keeping the mind of love even under the saw (MN 21).

name: Development of compassion (karuṇā)
method_summary: Pervading the directions with a mind of compassion; abandons cruelty (MN 62; DN 13).

name: Development of rejoicing (muditā)
method_summary: Pervading the directions with a mind of rejoicing; abandons discontent (MN 62; DN 13).

name: Development of equanimity (upekkhā)
method_summary: Pervading the directions with a mind of equanimity; abandons aversion (MN 62; DN 13).

name: Recollection of the Buddha
method_summary: Recollecting 'the Blessed One is an arahant, fully awakened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, well-farer, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed trainer, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed' (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)

name: Recollection of the Dhamma
method_summary: Recollecting 'the Dhamma is well proclaimed, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise' (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)

name: Recollection of the Saṅgha
method_summary: Recollecting the Saṅgha of the four pairs and eight persons as practising well, worthy of gifts and hospitality, an unsurpassed field of merit (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)

name: Recollection of one's virtue
method_summary: Recollecting one's own virtue as unbroken, untorn, liberating, praised by the wise (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)

name: Recollection of one's generosity
method_summary: Recollecting one's own generosity, living at home with a mind free of the stain of avarice (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)

name: Recollection of the deities
method_summary: Recollecting that the faith, virtue, learning, generosity and wisdom by which deities were reborn are present in oneself (AN 6.10).
signs_of_progress: the mind is not obsessed by lust, hatred or delusion; gladness, rapture, tranquillity, happiness and concentration arise (AN 6.10)

name: Perception of impermanence
method_summary: Attending to the impermanence of the aggregates and of all formations; it uproots the conceit 'I am' (MN 62; Ud 4.1) and is the first of the ten perceptions (AN 10.60).

name: The ten perceptions (Girimānanda)
method_summary: Impermanence, not-self, unattractiveness, danger, abandoning, dispassion, cessation, non-delight in the whole world, impermanence in all formations, mindfulness of breathing — recited to the sick (AN 10.60).

name: The five ways of removing distracting thoughts
method_summary: When unwholesome thoughts of desire, hatred or delusion arise: (1) attend to another, wholesome sign; (2) examine their danger; (3) forget and do not attend to them; (4) attend to stilling their source; (5) with teeth clenched and tongue on the palate, beat down mind with mind (MN 20).
signs_of_progress: mastery of the courses of thought: thinking what one wishes (MN 20)

name: Dividing thoughts into two classes
method_summary: Noting whether a thought is of sensuality, ill will or cruelty (to be abandoned) or of renunciation, good will or harmlessness (to be developed), since what one frequently thinks becomes the mind's inclination (MN 19).

name: Wise attention
method_summary: Attending to 'this is suffering … this is the way' rather than to questions about one's existence in past and future (MN 2); attending to the bases of the awakening factors and to the foulness sign to starve the hindrances (SN 46.51).

name: Sense restraint (indriyasaṃvara)
method_summary: Seeing a form with the eye (and so for each sense) one does not grasp at its signs and features, through which covetousness and grief might invade, but guards the faculty (DN 2; MN 27; MN 39); not blindness but quick equanimity (MN 152).

equivalents.note: Yoga's withdrawal of the senses; the Buddhist practice guards the senses while they function

name: Reflection before, during and after action; wise use of requisites
method_summary: Reflecting like looking in a mirror whether a bodily, verbal or mental act harms oneself or others (MN 61); using robes, alms-food, lodging and medicine wisely, for their purpose only (MN 2).

name: Moderation in eating
method_summary: Eating with reflection, not for amusement, intoxication or beautification, but to sustain the body and support the holy life (MN 39; MN 107).

name: Devotion to wakefulness
method_summary: Purifying the mind by walking and sitting through the day and the first and last watches of the night, lying down mindfully in the middle watch in the lion's posture (MN 39; MN 107).

name: Walking meditation (caṅkama)
method_summary: Walking back and forth with the senses turned inward and the mind not going outward (AN 7.61); by day and night as part of wakefulness (MN 39).

name: Patience (khanti)
method_summary: Enduring abuse, blows and even death without hatred (MN 21; MN 145); the sixth perfection.

name: Good friendship
method_summary: Associating with good friends and the wise, who are the whole of the holy life (SN 45.2; Ud 4.1; Snp 2.4).

name: Going for refuge
method_summary: Reciting three times 'I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the Dhamma, to the Saṅgha' (Khp 1); the entry to lay discipleship and once the form of ordination (Vin Mv 1.12).

name: The five precepts
method_summary: Undertaking to abstain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech and intoxicants — the five great gifts (AN 8.39).

equivalents.note: four of the five overlap with the yamas of YS 2.30; the Buddhist lists do not include the niyamas

name: The eight precepts
method_summary: On the uposatha, abstaining also from all sexual activity, eating after midday, entertainments and adornment, and high beds (AN 8.41).

name: The ten precepts
method_summary: The novice's ten training rules, adding the refusal of gold and silver (Khp 2).

name: Uposatha observance
method_summary: On the eighth, fourteenth and fifteenth of the fortnight lay followers keep the eight precepts and monks assemble to recite the Pātimokkha (AN 8.41; Vin Mv 2).

name: Recitation of the Pātimokkha
method_summary: The fortnightly recitation of the monastic code by the assembled Saṅgha on the uposatha, after purity has been declared (Vin Mv 2).

name: Full ordination
method_summary: Admission to the Saṅgha: first 'Come, monk', then by the three refuges, then by a formal act of the Saṅgha; for nuns by both Saṅghas (Vin Mv 1; Cv 10).

name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Giving to the virtuous, a dwelling for the Saṅgha of the four quarters, and regular gifts as sacrifices of great fruit (DN 5); the first perfection (Bv 2).

name: Offering on behalf of the departed
method_summary: Giving food and drink, especially to the Saṅgha, in the name of dead relatives, for their benefit (Khp 7 / Pv 1.5).

name: Protective recitation (paritta)
method_summary: Reciting protective discourses — the Āṭānāṭiya verses (DN 32), the Ratana and Mettā suttas, Aṅgulimāla's act of truth (MN 86) — for protection from non-human beings, illness and danger.

name: Act of truth (saccakiriyā)
method_summary: Declaring a truth about oneself or the Three Jewels and wishing for well-being by its power (MN 86; Snp 2.1).

name: Pilgrimage to the four places
method_summary: Visiting with a faithful heart the places of the Buddha's birth, awakening, first teaching and final nibbāna (DN 16).
signs_of_progress: dying on such a pilgrimage with a confident heart one is reborn in heaven (DN 16)

name: Caring for the sick
method_summary: Nursing sick fellow monks, as the Buddha did: 'whoever would attend on me should attend on the sick' (Vin Mv 8.26).

name: Ascetic practices (dhutaṅga)
method_summary: Voluntary austerities such as forest dwelling, living on alms-food only, wearing rag robes, living at the root of a tree — praised in Mahākassapa (Thag 18.1) and allowed as optional; the thirteen dhutaṅgas are listed in the commentaries (U37).

warnings.text: The Buddha refused Devadatta's demand to make forest dwelling, alms-food, rag robes, tree-root dwelling and abstaining from fish and meat compulsory for life; each is allowed only for those who wish.

name: Breathless meditation (appāṇaka jhāna)
method_summary: An austerity practised by the bodhisatta before his awakening, stopping the breath; the text records it only to reject it. No method is given here.

warnings.text: The bodhisatta experienced violent winds, pains and burning in the body; though his mind was not overpowered, he concluded that by this gruelling practice he did not attain superhuman knowledge and vision, and asked whether there might be another path to awakening.

name: Extreme reduction of food
method_summary: An austerity of living on minimal food practised by the bodhisatta and described in the texts only to reject it. No quantities or method are recorded here.

warnings.text: By this conduct and these austerities the bodhisatta did not attain superhuman distinction of knowledge and vision; he took solid food again (MN 12; MN 36).
